metadata.label: Monochrome
metadata.coverage: Twelve CISSCAL clear-filter observations in the Thomas controlled shape frame, including a regional ~100 m/pixel close frame with independently checked camera correction. Approximate disk correction and overlap levels reduce photographed illumination; shadows, variable resolution and marked gaps remain.

metadata.label: False color
metadata.coverage: Five Cassini pointings in IR3, IR1 and UV3, displayed as red, green and blue. Cameras use measured registration in the published shape frame; complete three-filter footprints are combined.

celestial.sunSource: JPL Saturn-system orbital data; the shape uses the controlled Cassini September 2005 frame. Its displayed orientation is arbitrary because Hyperion rotates chaotically.
celestial.qualification: The ephemeris locates the Sun, but Hyperion’s body attitude is an explicitly arbitrary display orientation. Its directional lighting is a display convention, not a prediction of the current tumbling surface phase.

facts.label: Discovery
facts.value: William Lassell and William and George Bond · 1848

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.notes: Twelve calibrated Cassini frames mapped to the irregular shape, including a regional close view sampled at about 100 m/pixel. Registration and shape uncertainty limit detail; crater shadows remain, coverage varies and gaps are marked.

controls.label: False color
controls.notes: Five Cassini pointings in IR3, IR1 and UV3, displayed as red, green and blue. Cameras use measured registration in the published shape frame; complete three-filter footprints are combined.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.notes: Radius above a 135 km reference sphere from the Cassini stereo and limb shape model. This shows global relief and elongation, not a finely resolved terrain DEM; shape uncertainty reaches 6 km on the less-observed side.

resources.label: NASA/JPL/SSI; PDS
resources.description: Cassini ISS calibrated observations and Thomas controlled shape

physical.credit: Vendored JPL physical and orbital data

excludedTypeCodes.AL: Telescopic albedo features carry no Gazetteer diameter and describe historic shading, not mapped landforms.
